name: Claret Violet
lede: Claret Violet is a very dark purplish red, one of the few colors in our library traced to the German RAL industrial standard rather than an English color dictionary.

sections.title: A wine word, by way of a German standard
sections.body:
Our library's only source for Claret Violet is the RAL color standard, catalogued in 1927 as RAL 4004, a screen approximation of that swatch [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would place it in block 259, dark purplish red, 4.7 units from that block's centroid [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[bokhara]], [[merlot]], [[tyrian-purple]] and [[pansy-purple]], at 2.6, 2.9, 
The name joins *claret*, the English word for a dark red Bordeaux wine, with *violet* for its purple cast; it shares its first word with [[claret]] itself, a lighter, redder color in our library [1][2]. In feel it sits between [[merlot]] and [[burgundy]], two other wine-named reds in our data [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Claret Violet covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only one work, a *Saint Jerome* dated around 1600, as photographed [3]. Such a dark, specific purplish red rarely covers enough of a varnished, aged canvas to register at this threshold, so its near-absence here says more about the archive's photography than about the color's history [3].
